issue: The maxIterations row says: 'Under --depth-mode=expansive a `default` budget is resized after the seed step to `min(24, max(10, 2·c·(S + maxDepth − 1)))`, with S the depth-1 nodes the seed admitted and c = 1; any other source is kept as given'. It does not limit this to single-executor runs. In a fan-out run the parent budget is never resized. fanout-run.cjs expansiveLineageBudgets (lines 332-350) sizes each lineage that has no matrix iterations value from its own round-robin share of the open depth-1 seed nodes (partitionFrontierNodes, lines 312-322), not from the whole seed. The floor is 12 for a native lineage and the workflow default of 10 for a CLI lineage, and a lineage dealt no seed node runs at that floor. Only a matrix iterations value is kept as given. The yaml's fan-out seed step (deep-research.yaml line 359) passes no --max-iterations-source, and step_fanout_spawn_cli passes no max-iterations value to fanout-run.cjs. Its FANOUT_FLAGS list (lines 30-36) has no maxIterations entry. So a --max-iterations flag or marker is not kept as given for fan-out lineages. A fan-out reader gets the wrong set of nodes, the wrong floor and the wrong rule for which sources are kept.

issue: The custom-dimension rubric row says a configured custom dimension "is not required for severity coverage". The code does require it. step_normalize_review_dimensions (yaml 830-831) keeps custom names in config.reviewDimensions, and the registry seed (yaml 1027) writes "<custom>":false. convergence.cjs 1599-1614 then builds missingDimensions from config.reviewDimensions, so dimensionCoverageGate fails and the all_dimensions_clean candidate (cleanReviewStop, convergence.cjs 1127-1132) cannot form until the custom dimension is covered. Under expansive depth, reduce-state.cjs buildReviewFrontier (1997-2015) also marks a node answered only once every name in buildDimensionUniverse has evidence, and that universe includes the custom names. The reducer has no four-only coverage check that "severity coverage" could refer to: REQUIRED_DIMENSIONS is only the starting point of buildDimensionUniverse. So the doc presents custom dimensions as optional when they block the stop.

critic_override.note: 'Severity coverage' is a defined contract term, not a claim about the stop gate. deep-review/assets/review-mode-contract.yaml:69-92 sets requiredForSeverityCoverage true only for correctness and security. It sets it false for traceability, maintainability and customDimensionRule, yet traceability and maintainability also block all_dimensions_clean. The only code that reads the flag is render-contract-snapshot.cjs:301. So the yaml:2645 row is true under the contract and matches custom-review-dimensions.md:16 and feature-catalog.md:440. It does not say custom dimensions are optional for the stop, so it does not mislead a reader into a wrong stop. The real gap is that the row leaves out that the custom dimension still gates the clean stop (convergence.cjs:1599-1614, :1127-1132). That is a clarity follow-up, so P2.

issue: step_extend_completed_run on_fail says "Exit 2 is a usage error, such as a run that is not complete ... Any other failure halts with STATUS=FAIL". The command at line 588 ends the inline node script with `|| { rm -rf "$WORK_DIR"; exit 2; }`. That turns every failure of the script into exit 2 and so into the usage-error branch: an unparseable config, an unreadable state log, a JSON.parse throw. Only the gateway append (line 589) and the config mv (line 590) exit 1. A corrupt config or a missing state log is therefore reported as a usage error, not as STATUS=FAIL.

issue: The doc says the template defines `antiConvergence.minIterations` and 'The workflow writes those values into the config record'. That implies the run's floor lives at `antiConvergence.minIterations`. In fact `step_create_config` in deep-research.yaml writes the floor as a top-level `minIterations: 3` (line 723), and `stopDecisionConfig` in convergence.cjs (lines 1398-1400) reads `config.minIterations` before `antiConvergence.minIterations`. So editing `antiConvergence.minIterations` in a created config does not change the floor while the top-level key is present. The doc should name the top-level `minIterations` key the workflow writes and say that it takes precedence.

disposition.note: Not this program's: deep-research/feature-catalog/convergence/anti-convergence-floor.md, the top-level minIterations: 3 that step_create_config writes in deep-research.yaml, and the precedence in convergence.cjs stopDecisionConfig all predate the program base 21c4b325b5a, and the catalog entry has no diff since then. Owner: the deep-research feature catalog (convergence group). The finding stands: the entry should name the top-level minIterations key the workflow writes and say it is read before antiConvergence.minIterations.
